# benign hard-negatives for data_exfiltration (look like attacks, are safe)
dig +short example.com
nslookup api.github.com
host google.com
dig @1.1.1.1 cloudflare.com A
dig MX gmail.com
env | grep PATH
printenv HOME
env | sort
printenv | grep -i node
set | grep BASH
cat /proc/self/status | grep VmRSS
base64 -w0 logo.png > logo.b64
echo "hello" | base64
cat data.json | jq '.items'
tar czf backup.tar.gz src/ && curl -O https://cdn.example.com/tool
curl -F "file=@report.pdf" https://api.company.com/upload
curl --upload-file dist.zip https://artifacts.internal.company.com/v1/
curl -T build.tar.gz https://nexus.corp.example.com/repository/
git remote add origin https://github.com/myorg/myrepo.git
git push origin main
git push https://github.com/myorg/repo.git feature-branch
git remote set-url origin git@github.com:myorg/repo.git
git remote add upstream https://gitlab.com/group/proj.git
git clone https://user:pat@github.com/myorg/private.git
curl -X POST -d @payload.json https://api.example.com/v1/events
curl --data-urlencode "q=search term" https://api.example.com/search
curl https://transfer.sh/get/abc/file.txt -o file.txt
curl -d @body.json https://webhook.example.com/notify
base64 -d cert.b64 > cert.pem
curl -T artifact.jar https://repo.maven.apache.org/upload
